description.narrative:
För att den colombianska ekonomin ska växa hållbart och bryta ojämlikheterna i dagens system, möta utmaningarna på morgondagens arbetsmarknad samt övervinna årtionden av konflikter som har splittrat samhället, är förändringar på arbetsmarknaden nödvändiga. Sådan utveckling är starkt beroende av en förändring av kultur och uppfattningar, inte bara i dialogen mellan arbetsgivare och fackföreningar, utan inom dessa grupper och organisationer själva. Under projektet “Private Sector contribution to Social Dialogue in Colombia", avser NIR att stärka denna dialogen genom att bygga förtroende och ge tillgång till verktyg bland aktörer på olika nivåer på arbetsmarknaden.
Detta två och ett halvårsprojekt avser vidare att stödja Colombias genomförandeprocessen av Colombias nyligen godkända OECD medlemskap genom att addressera de behov som identifierats i de senaste OECD-bedömningarna beträffande Colombias arbetsmarknad.
Projektet fokuserar på tre komponenter; att skapa ett arbetsmarknadsdialoginitiativ, att utveckla medlingsmekanismen på arbetsmarknaden samt att utforma ett arbetsplatsprogram för sociala dialog på arbetsmarknadens - alla aktiviteter delar ett långsiktigt mål, att uppnå en bättre kapacitet för en hållbar social dialog. Projektet börjar med en första fas på sex månader för att säkerställa att de specifika aktiviteterna utvecklas i nära samarbete med lokala intressenter.

This project “Private Sector contribution to Social Dialogue in Colombia", intends to support Colombia’s OECD implementation process by addressing needs identified in the recent OECD assessments of the labour market. The project focuses on two components; to create a labour market dialogue initiative and to develop the mediation mechanism for the labour market at firm level. The implementing partner is the International Council of Swedish Industry (NIR) who intends to strengthen the dialogue through building trust and providing access to tools among actors at different levels at the labour market.

The aim of the programme Private Sector contribution to Social Dialogue in Colombia is to provide improved conditions for a Sustainable Social Dialogue. The program targeted social dialogue on three levels; social dialogue among the labour market parties at 1) central, regional and sectoral level 2) the company and firm level and 3) the workplace level. The combination of these tracks is intended to be mutually reinforcing, and to provide several avenues to achieve results. Thus, strengthening the dialogue through building trust and providing access to tools among actors at different levels in the labour market. Hence, the project initially focused on three components: to create a labour market dialogue initiative; to develop the mediation mechanism for the labour market at firm level; as well as to design local social dialogue workplace programs - all activities with a shared long-term outcome; to achieve an improved capacity for a sustainable social dialogue.
During the first six months of the project implementation period, NIR and the Swedish Trade Union Federation IF Metall started a global social dialogue programme called the Swedish Workplace Programme (SWP) financed by Sida, Contribution No 12919. After discussions with Sida, NIR decided to integrate the third component into SWP, thus removing that outcome from this project.

Regarding the first output, which aims at putting in place an operational structure for future dialogue between the government, the three main national Trade Unions and employers (represented by ANDI) as part of the OECD agenda, the Embassy's assessment is that progress was very limited during the whole activity period.
In early 2019, the former Colombian Ambassador to the OECD, Catalina Crane, was hired as Coordinator. Catalina Crane had both individual and joint meetings, as part of the parallel dialogue apart from with the Commission for Labour Concertation which is an official tri partite forum. Her experience and general recognition among the parties facilitated dialogue and the Trade Unions and ANDI finally agreed to prioritize: informality and its relation to both productivity and job stability as the topic to discuss during the year. The objective was to present a joint position with recommendations to the government. However, by the end of the year this bilateral dialogue was suspended because of the different perspectives of ANDI and the Unions regarding Colombian Governmental reforms to the pension system and labour legislation.
When the Coronavirus pandemic reached Colombia in March 2020, the country went into a rapid lock-down and all political effort was redirected to the handling of the pandemic.
The polarized context caused by the massive popular opposition to the governmental proposed tax reform, impeded any dialogue during the first half of 2021. The three main trade unions joined the National Strike Committee and protests continued during April and May 2021 leading to violent clashes with the National police.
NIR visited Bogota in October 2021 and met with the three trade unions, ANDI and the Ministry of Labour. All three sides confirmed the difficulties of trying to re-establish a dialogue between all parties. The combination of the on-going protests and the pandemic restrictions made progress difficult and after an analysis of the situation and consultations with all involved actors and the approval from Sida, NIR decided to cancel the activities related to this component. However, despite their obvious frustration with Andi and the Government, the Trade Unions participated in the Global Deal event held in Cartagena on November the 25th and 26th, 2021. Representatives from NIR, some Swedish companies (Electrolux, SKF, Securitas and Scania), Swedish Trade Union (LO) also participated together with the Swedish Ambassador. The General Director for Trade from the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs opened the event together with the OECD Secretary General and the ILO Director General. The Swedish Ambassador closed the event by emphasizing the importance of fostering democratic institutions, protecting human rights defenders, promoting business formalization and promoting the participation of employees in decisions taken by companies as important steps for promoting social dialogue. NIR contributed to this event by attracting Swedish company participation and by talking about the first years experience of the Swedish workplace program.
Regarding the second output, which aims at reactivating a resource pool of mediators, the Embassy's assessment is that NIR made progress in 2021 and 2022. The mediation component is recognized by all stakeholders as a possible way forward to help improve relations between employers and employees and is seen as a good alternative to the current practice of addressing labour conflicts through lengthy judicial processes. The alliance with Universidad Javeriana has opened new opportunities as it is an actor outside the social dialogue but one that is recognized by all parties (Ministry of Labour, employers and employees).
Despite some delays due to the Covid 19 restrictions, three seminars on Alternative Conflict Resolution Mechanisms (MASC is its acronym in Spanish), research and a course on mediation, were the main activities undertaken in 2021. The results of the seminars and research were presented by Javeriana in the Global Deal event in Cartagena on November the 26th, 2021. The Embassy's assessment is that this second component made significant progress thanks to the alliance with Javeriana University.
In 2023, the final product delivered by Javeriana University was a proposal for a Mediation Institute including necessary legal reforms and the institutional set-up and this was presented to the Colombian government. The Vice-Minister of Labour confirmed the governments commitment to the proposal as part of the overall reform agenda for the labour market. A presentation of the proposal was made to several potential international donors together with the Swedish Ambassador in February 2023 and then the activity period ended by the end of April 2023.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
